purpose: Make release-train, fixed-group, linked-group, prerelease, and stable-release interactions explicit before adding orchestration that could produce competing version authority.
scope: A normative release-lane policy document at docs/07-lane-policy.md, plus a small set of net-new cross-lane validation checks and planner-determinism codification for the existing version planner (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs). Covers: (a) authoring the lane-authority-precedence documentation (AC-001) and codifying already-shipped fixed/linked-group conflict detection as normative (AC-002) -- these two are pure documentation tracks with no new code; (b) net-new validation logic for prerelease-lane vs. group conflicts (AC-002a, new GraphError::PrereleaseGroupConflict, E123) and abandoned-prerelease-lane gating (AC-003, AC-003b), both of which require a new `abandoned: bool` field on `PreState` (crates/callisto-format/src/pre.rs), a corresponding read/write path in `parse_pre_json`/`write_pre_json`, and a new rejection path (GraphError::AbandonedPrereleaseLane, E124) in the planner; (c) a determinism test asserting `plan_version`'s serialized output is byte-for-byte stable across two consecutive invocations (AC-004), which is independently verifiable and touches no planner internals beyond adding a test -- it stays bundled in this spec as a distinct, self-contained track rather than a separate one.
non_goals: Implementing a full release-train scheduler or time-based calendar.
Changing existing fixed- or linked-group version semantics without an approved follow-on specification.
Inferring organization-specific release cadence from package names or branch names.
Re-validating or duplicating the fixed/linked-group membership conflict detection already implemented in crates/callisto-graph/src/config/groups.rs (GraphError::ConflictingGroupMembership, E109).

Introducing a per-package prerelease lane model. The existing prerelease lane (.changeset/pre.json, parsed by callisto_format::parse_pre_json into PreState) is a single workspace-scoped lane whose membership is the packages listed in PreState.initial_versions; this spec documents and constrains that existing model rather than replacing it with a per-package one.

Building any UI, CLI subcommand, or automation for clearing an abandoned prerelease lane. This spec only requires that planning reject an abandoned lane's affected packages with a diagnostic; the operator clears it today via manual edit of .changeset/pre.json (setting `abandoned` back to false or absent) or deletion of the file, which is unchanged by this spec.

Adding a VersionOptions field (e.g. a `stable_publish` flag) to distinguish 'stable release intent' from 'prerelease accumulation intent' at the plan_version call boundary. Investigation of the real call sites (crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/version.rs:14-25, the sole non-test caller of plan_version besides crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs and pr_body.rs, which pass VersionOptions::default() or CLI flags unrelated to lane state) found exactly one CLI entry point with no such distinction today, and none is needed: plan_version's existing PreMode-driven behavior (PreMode::Pre produces a prerelease-tagged bump; PreMode::Exit finalizes to stable, per the already-shipped synthetic-severity injection at crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs:104-115) already fully determines what version shape a given invocation produces. There is no reachable 'attempt a stable release while the lane is still in PreMode::Pre' pathway to gate, because a PreMode::Pre invocation cannot produce a stable version in the first place -- it always produces a prerelease-tagged one. AC-003/AC-003b therefore gate on PreState.abandoned alone, not on PreMode, and not on any new intent field.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: docs/07-lane-policy.md names, for every package at a given planning point, exactly one authority responsible for selecting that package's next version: the package itself (independent lane), its fixed group, its linked group, or the workspace's prerelease lane (as defined by .changeset/pre.json). The document states the precedence for all six unordered pairs among these four authority kinds, with no pairing left undecided: (1) independent x fixed group -- mutually exclusive by construction: GroupTable::resolve (crates/callisto-graph/src/config/groups.rs:127-222) tracks every package claimed by any fixed or linked group in a single shared `claimed_by: BTreeMap<PackageId, GroupName>` map spanning both the fixed and linked resolution loops, so a package resolved into `fixed_of` cannot simultaneously be `ungrouped` -- it is either a member of exactly one group (fixed or linked) or of none. (2) independent x linked group -- mutually exclusive by the same construction. (3) fixed group x linked group -- mutually exclusive: the shared `claimed_by` map means a package claimed by a fixed group that is also named in a linked group's member list is rejected at config-resolution time via GraphError::ConflictingGroupMembership (E109), per AC-002, before any planning proceeds -- this holds even when the colliding raw member names differ syntactically (e.g. a bare name vs. a scoped alias resolving to the same PackageId via IdentityIndex::resolve_human), not only for literal string duplicates. (4) independent x prerelease lane -- MAY apply concurrently: an independent package (one with neither `fixed_of` nor `linked_of` set) may be listed in PreState.initial_versions; when active, the prerelease lane's mode (PreMode::Pre or PreMode::Exit) takes precedence over independent inference for shaping the package's target version (prerelease tag application while accumulating, or finalization to stable on exit), though the package's own inferred severity still feeds the lane's bump as input. (5) fixed group x prerelease lane -- MUST NOT apply concurrently; rejected per AC-002a. (6) linked group x prerelease lane -- MUST NOT apply concurrently; rejected per AC-002a. The document states as a corollary that a package's prerelease-lane membership can only ever coexist with the independent authority kind, never with fixed or linked group membership, because (5) and (6) are hard rejections.

docs/07-lane-policy.md codifies the fixed/linked-group membership conflict detection already implemented in GroupTable::resolve (crates/callisto-graph/src/config/groups.rs:127-222) as normative: a package listed as a member of two conflicting fixed or linked groups is rejected during config resolution via GraphError::ConflictingGroupMembership, with a diagnostic naming the package and both conflicting group names (the group already recorded in `claimed_by` and the new group attempting to claim the same PackageId), before any planning proceeds. This criterion documents existing, already-shipped and already-tested behavior (crates/callisto-graph/tests/config_resolve_tests.rs) and requires no new detection logic.

This spec adds a new GraphError variant, `PrereleaseGroupConflict { package: PackageId, group: GroupName, lane_tag: String }`, with diagnostic code E123 (the next unused sequential code after the highest currently assigned code, E122, in crates/callisto-graph/src/error.rs; E112 is a pre-existing gap in the sequence and is deliberately not reused, since its retirement is undocumented and reuse risks colliding with a prior meaning). The check is net-new: no existing code in crates/callisto-graph checks for a prerelease-lane vs. fixed/linked-group conflict. It is added to plan_version (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs) immediately after pre_state is loaded (after the block at lines 79-86) and before the CascadeInput is constructed (line 117) or run_cascade executes (line 134). For every package in the workspace that has either `ws.config.groups.fixed_of` or `ws.config.groups.linked_of` set (i.e. is a member of a fixed or linked group) AND whose package name (`PackageId::name()`, matching the resolution convention already used at crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs:430 and crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs:285 to key into `PreState.initial_versions`) is a key in the active `pre_state.initial_versions` (pre_state is Some), plan_version returns `Err(GraphError::PrereleaseGroupConflict)` naming that package, its conflicting group name (from `fixed_of` or `linked_of`, whichever is set), and `pre_state.tag`, before manifest, tag, changelog, or registry mutation. This is the only conformant behavior -- there is no precedence-based subordination path, and no configuration can make this pairing succeed. This check runs before AC-003/AC-003b's per-package lane-state check: if a package trips both AC-002a (group conflict) and AC-003 (abandoned-lane gating), AC-002a's rejection is the one that fires and planning halts for that package on the group-conflict diagnostic; AC-003/AC-003b are never reached for that package. This ordering holds because AC-002a's check runs earlier in plan_version's control flow (immediately after pre_state is loaded), structurally prior to AC-003/AC-003b's evaluation, which only makes sense to run on packages that already passed group-conflict screening.

This spec adds a net-new `abandoned: bool` field to `PreState` (crates/callisto-format/src/pre.rs), serialized as an optional top-level JSON key named `abandoned`. `parse_pre_json` (crates/callisto-format/src/pre.rs:43-113), which is a hand-rolled parser building `PreState` field-by-field from a `serde_json::Value` (not a `#[derive(Deserialize)]` path), reads this key as follows: if `obj.get("abandoned")` is absent, `PreState.abandoned` is `false`; if present and `.as_bool()` returns `Some(b)`, `PreState.abandoned` is `b`; if present and not a JSON boolean, parsing fails with `PreJsonError::WrongFieldType { field: "abandoned" }` (the existing variant, reused rather than adding a new one, consistent with how every other typed field in this parser reports a type mismatch). `write_pre_json` (crates/callisto-format/src/pre.rs:115-133) writes the `"abandoned"` key into the output map only when `state.abandoned == true`; when `false`, the key is omitted entirely, so the existing round-trip test `pre_json_round_trips` (which asserts a written pre.json with no `abandoned` key reproduces its input byte-for-byte) continues to pass unmodified. A parser-level test exists for each of: key absent (`abandoned == false`), key present as `true`, key present as `false`, key present as a non-boolean JSON value (`WrongFieldType` returned, field name `"abandoned"`). `abandoned` is settable only by direct edit of `.changeset/pre.json` (no CLI support is added by this spec, per non_goals).

For a given package, evaluated only after that package has cleared AC-002a's group-conflict check (a package rejected by AC-002a is never evaluated against this criterion), the sole discriminator for this criterion is `pre_state.abandoned` -- not `PreMode`, and not any new `VersionOptions` field (see non_goals for why no such field is introduced). Immediately after AC-002a's check in plan_version, for every package whose name is a key in the active `pre_state.initial_versions` (pre_state is Some) and `pre_state.abandoned == true`, plan_version returns `Err(GraphError::AbandonedPrereleaseLane { package: PackageId, lane_tag: String })` (a new GraphError variant, diagnostic code E124, the next sequential code after AC-002a's E123), naming the package and `pre_state.tag`, with a diagnostic/help message directing the operator to clear the abandoned lane (delete .changeset/pre.json or edit `abandoned` back to `false`) before planning can proceed for that package, before manifest, tag, changelog, or registry mutation. This holds regardless of `PreMode` (Pre or Exit) -- an abandoned lane is blocked in either mode, since neither accumulating further prereleases nor finalizing to stable is a sensible operation on a lane the operator has marked abandoned. A test exists asserting this rejection for a package listed in `initial_versions` with `abandoned == true`, in both PreMode::Pre and PreMode::Exit.

Given a package that cleared AC-002a (no group conflict) and is not rejected by AC-003 (`pre_state.abandoned` is not `true` for it), plan_version permits planning to proceed for that package in every one of the following starting states, with no new rejection introduced by this spec: (1) no prerelease lane active -- `.changeset/pre.json` does not exist (`pre_state` is `None`) -- planning proceeds using ordinary independent/group severity inference, unaffected by any lane. (2) prerelease lane active, package's name is a key in `PreState.initial_versions`, `abandoned == false`, `mode == PreMode::Pre` -- planning proceeds and produces a prerelease-tagged bump for the package (already-shipped behavior, unchanged by this spec: the lane is actively accumulating, and continuing to accumulate is the lane's normal, expected operation, not a condition to block). (3) prerelease lane active, package's name is a key in `PreState.initial_versions`, `abandoned == false`, `mode == PreMode::Exit` -- planning proceeds and finalizes the package's prerelease version to stable (this codifies the already-shipped synthetic-severity-injection behavior at crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs:104-115 as normative, not new logic). (4) prerelease lane active, but the package's name is NOT a key in `PreState.initial_versions` (the lane is workspace-scoped per non_goals and routinely covers only a subset of packages; plan_version's synthetic-severity-injection loop at crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs:106 iterates every package in `base_versions`, i.e. every package in the workspace, filtering by `ver.is_prerelease()`, not by lane membership -- so packages outside the lane are still planned in the same run) -- planning proceeds identically to case (1): the lane does not govern this package, so its absence from `initial_versions` is equivalent to no lane being active for it. An automated test exists for each of the four states above asserting plan_version returns `Ok` (no rejection) for the package under evaluation, with case (2) asserting the resulting bump carries a prerelease-tagged version and case (3) asserting it carries a finalized stable version.

Given identical source tree contents, configuration files, and inputs to plan_version (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs), two consecutive invocations of plan_version in the same process produce VersionPlan values whose VersionPlan::to_report(None) output (the `lockfiles` parameter, of type Option<Vec<LockfileRefreshResult>> per crates/callisto-graph/src/plan.rs:65, is passed as None on both invocations, keeping the comparison hermetic and independent of lockfile-refresh side effects that are irrelevant to planner determinism), serialized via serde_json::to_string, is byte-for-byte identical -- covering both the bumps list (including per-bump ordering) and the diagnostics list (including diagnostic ordering). An automated test added to the existing `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block in crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs:356-357) builds one fixture workspace using that module's existing tempdir + git_init_with_commit helper pattern (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs:379, as already used by test_plan_version_produces_correct_bumps_in_cascade), calls plan_version twice against that same fixture workspace without any mutation between calls, and asserts the two serde_json::to_string(&plan.to_report(None)) outputs are equal.

revision_note: Full rewrite from scratch (not an incremental patch) after 3 rounds of canon:exit-gate failures on the prior version. Key changes from the prior (round-3-failing) draft: (1) AC-003's fabricated 'stable-lane publish' trigger discriminator is removed entirely -- investigation of the real call sites (crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/version.rs, the only non-test plan_version caller besides publish.rs/pr_body.rs) found no field or signal distinguishing 'stable-lane publish intent' from 'prerelease accumulation intent', and none is needed, because PreMode alone already fully determines the shape of a permitted continuation (Pre -> prerelease bump, Exit -> finalization) -- there is no reachable case where a Pre-mode invocation produces a stable version, so there was never a real scenario for the old case (4) to gate. (2) AC-003 is split into AC-003 (the sole remaining gate: `abandoned == true` blocks unconditionally, regardless of PreMode) and AC-003b (four PERMITTED continuation states, replacing the old 5-state single criterion), removing the contradiction between the old scoping clause and its own case (2). (3) AC-003's `abandoned` field now specifies parse_pre_json's real hand-rolled (non-serde-derive) read path precisely: an optional top-level `abandoned` boolean key, absent maps to false, non-boolean maps to the existing PreJsonError::WrongFieldType{field:"abandoned"} variant -- with parser-level tests for all four cases -- and write_pre_json's write path is specified to omit the key when false, preserving the existing pre_json_round_trips test unmodified. (4) AC-002a now names its new GraphError variant (PrereleaseGroupConflict), its fields, and its assigned code (E123, the next unused sequential code after E122; the E112 gap is deliberately not reused). AC-003 similarly names AbandonedPrereleaseLane and E124. (5) AC-001's group-mutual-exclusivity claim (pairs 1-3) is re-grounded against the actual shared `claimed_by` map in GroupTable::resolve, which spans both the fixed and linked resolution loops -- confirmed to catch cross-kind identity collisions, not just literal string duplicates. (6) AC-004 is carried forward unchanged from the round-2 fix, which already correctly named VersionPlan::to_report's real signature and a concrete fixture pattern; it was not implicated in the round-3 failure.
